findings.detail: X02 is firing on source N/A interest-rate rows with no principal or fair value, not on rows where a rate exists but was missed.

rationale: The raw filing's schedule columns are Investment Type, Spread Above Index, Interest Rate, Maturity Date, Principal, Amortized Cost, Percentage of Net Assets, and Fair Value. The flagged examples are private-credit rows where the source itself prints N/A(6) in the Interest Rate column, leaves the spread cells blank, and shows dash principal and fair value with only small negative amortized-cost adjustments. Adjacent same-issuer rows carry normal spread/rate terms, e.g. ABC Legal Holdings row 9 has SF + 4.50% and 8.34%, so the missing-rate warning is a rule-scope false alarm for intentional N/A adjustment rows rather than a stored data error.
